answer: Make every identity earn its place each epoch by answering a task it did not write. The protocol pairs a newcomer with a random established peer who hand-authors a fresh problem — decode this harbor chart, or find the pearl hidden among sparrow-track clues. Because the challenger sits outside your control, a sybil ring cannot self-feed scripted replies to itself. Faking N clones then means genuinely solving N externally-authored puzzles every single epoch — a linear, recurring cognitive cost per fake, not one mint cheaply copied.
